In this petition, petitioner is seeking grant of bail for the offences punishable under Sections 323,
506, 400, 420 read with Section 34 of Ipc in CC.No.516/2016 (crime No.208/2012) on the file of
Jmf
C, (II Court), Mangalore.

2. Heard the arguments Sri. K. Ravishankar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.N.Anitha Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader.
3.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the case was registered in the year 2012.
The petitioner was not aware of filing of the charge sheet in CC.No.2245/2014 and he was not served with the summons.
For this reason case was split against him and registered in CC.No.516/2014 and he was declared as proclaimed offender and the case was transferred to LPC.No.18/2022.
After coming to know about the case, the petitioner was appeared before the police and he was arrested under NBW and subjected to judicial NC: 2023:KHC:37711 custody.
The petitioner is ready to face the Trial and by imposing any conditions he may be granted bail.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader contended that the petitioner had committed the crime of breach of trust against the complainant in the year 2011.
In spite of service of summons he did not appear before the Court and avoided the Court process, ultimately he was declared as proclaimed offender and case was transferred to long pending register.
With great difficulty his presence was secured, if bail is granted he will again abscond and sought for rejection of the petition.
5. I gave my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

6. The charge against the petition is that he received a sum of Rs.4,50,000/- from Dr. Prakash Shetty on the ground that there is a land available at Mannagudde of Sulthan Batheri and executed an agreement.
He did not execute the sale deed and thereby cheated the complainant.
When the complainant approached the petitioner for refund of money, it was not NC: 2023:KHC:37711 returned, rather he was physically assaulted with criminal intimidation.
The complaint was registered in Crime No.208/2012 culminated in filing of the charge sheet in CC.No.2245/2016.

sentences.text:
now his presence was secured under NBW.
7.

The material on record also point out that matter was proceeded against accused No.2 /
Sri.Srinivasa Nayak.
Who has challenged the charge sheet before this Court in Crl.P.No.2916/2019 and vide order dated 09.03.2023 the charge sheet against the accused No.2 was quashed by this Court.
Now their remain the trial of the case against the petitioner, who come forward to face the trial.

The reasons assigned for not appearing before the Court is that, soon after the alleged incident the petitioner has shifted to Bangalore for doing business and he was un-aware of the proceedings before the Trial Court.
There is no dispute that the petitioner is a permanent resident of Mangalore and he has deep roots in the local society.

Having regard to the gravity of the offence of the alleged incident took place in the year 2011, I am of the opinion that it is not proper to keep the petitioner in jail as pre trial conviction and by imposing conditions discretion may be exercised in his favour.
The petitioner has undertaken to abide any conditions that would be imposed against him.
Conditions will meet the apprehension of the prosecution.
Hence the petition deserves merit consideration.

In the result, the following;
ORDER (i) Petition is allowed.

(ii) The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail on executing personal bond of sum of Rs.50,000/- and a surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the learned Magistrate subject to following conditions.
iii) The petitioner shall appear before Court regularly and face the trial.
iv) He shall assist the Court in disposal of the Trial as early as possible.
v) The petitioner shall furnish his Bangalore address before the Magistrate.
NC: 2023:KHC:37711 vi) The petitioner shall clear the bond amount, which was forfeited to state by the Trial Court.
